description: Compute the exponent of the multiplicative unit group modulo n using prime-power decomposition and an LCM.

source.title: Carmichael's lambda-function, Notes 7: Public-key cryptography, Theorem 22
source.author: Richard A. Wilson
source.publisher: Queen Mary University of London, MAS 335 Cryptography notes
source.reference: Theorem 22(a-c), Carmichael prime-power values and least-common-multiple composition

output.encoding: Carmichael lambda(n), the least positive exponent e such that a^e=1 modulo n for every a coprime to n

contract.prime_power_values: For odd prime p, lambda(p^a)=p^(a-1)*(p-1); lambda(2)=1; lambda(4)=2; for a>=3, lambda(2^a)=2^(a-2)
contract.composition: If n is a product of coprime prime powers, lambda(n) is the least common multiple of their lambda values
contract.primary_method: Trial-factor n, compute one lambda value per prime-power factor, then fold with lcm
contract.independent_method: Enumerate every unit residue modulo n, compute its multiplicative order by repeated multiplication, then take the lcm of all orders
contract.distinction: This returns the unit-group exponent, not Euler's unit count phi(n) and not a Carmichael-number predicate
contract.invalid_cases: Null, non-exact frame, n below 1, or n above 1024 returns -1

complexity.primary_time: O(sqrt(n)) trial divisions, plus O(r log n) gcd/LCM work for r distinct prime factors
complexity.independent_time: O(n^2) modular multiplications in the worst case
